## Current contract and formula ownership

The raw owner inventory below is interpreted as current fact, not target capability:

- `RawCaptureFrameView::retained_bytes(&self) -> usize` is the only domain frame-size seam. It is
  collapsed and infallible. `CaptureAuthorityBundle` has no retained-size method.
- Bounded identity primitives report `String::capacity()`, while sources separately approximate Arc
  control storage. Production, diagnostic, and both test-frame owners use coarse independent totals;
  they use lengths, saturation, `usize::MAX`, or omit reachable allocations. Diagnostic and test
  bundle graphs currently have no bundle-retained formula.
- Resident identity allocations are cloned into health events/snapshots and identity-bearing
  generation/control errors without a shared accounted token. Successor state and identity
  allocations are also unreserved.
- `raw_capture_channel` uses `std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel`, including its 64-slot health
  channel. It has no observed-slot fixed formula, fallible allocation, unified authoritative total,
  resident-generation token, or process-infrastructure proof.
- Current queue accounting is only per-record `queued_bytes`, quoted as
  `frame.retained_bytes() + size_of::<CaptureMessage<B>>()`. It double-funds the inline frame,
  charges resident data per record, omits conversion overlap, and cannot prove payload identity.
- Writer-owned formatting/event scratch vectors, source Arc, lifecycle Arcs/Mutex/Notify, thread
  name/spawn/control, handle state, and destination lease are unquoted and unreserved. Writer
  conversion and `RawCaptureRecord::try_new_live` each copy payload bytes; reservation drops before
  conversion, append, and triggered flush.
- The process destination registry is a lazy growable `HashMap`; its lease Arc/weak-reference
  lifetime, entries, and backing allocation have no process ledger or permanent Ready/Failed state.
- The current `CaptureSink` trait declares no retention-budget contract. `JournalWriter` uses
  `serde_json::to_vec` and has no fixed ledger. `MemoryCaptureSink::default()` retains clones in
  a growable vector with no count/byte ceiling.
- The authoritative current live payload ceiling is
  `RawCaptureRecord::MAX_LIVE_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024`; compatibility reads retain their
  separate historical limit.

The frozen plan's checked fixed/resident/record/sink formulas remain implementation obligations. No
current coarse value is treated as proof of that future graph.

## Hidden migration owners outside headline counts

The executable inventories establish these mandatory ripple owners:

- Channel definition/export; trusted-time factory definition; `CaptureContext`; publisher
  `Clone`; both sender clones; and both positive publisher-`Clone` assertions.
- Domain capture/identity contracts, private source Arc estimate, bounded payload allocation,
  production binding/frame/lease/bundle, diagnostic frame/bundle and shared atomic graph, and both
  domain/platform test frame/bundle graphs.
- Capture state/control, health/snapshot/error/successor identities, writer scratch/conversion/start/
  runtime/lifecycle, raw records and both payload copies, journal, destination registry/lease, all
  11 production/test sink implementations, configuration precedence, application composition, and
  source supervision.
- Every `journal_queue_capacity` file/environment/override/accessor/default/test owner, including
  `MARKET_SQUAWK_JOURNAL_QUEUE_CAPACITY`, migrates atomically to the three frozen fields with
  legacy spelling rejection.
